seeds.old: where user_id = ${userId} and token_hash != ${exceptTokenHash} and revoked_at is null
seeds.new: where token_hash != ${exceptTokenHash} and revoked_at is null
seeds.desc: Postgres revokeUserSessions drops the user_id predicate, so one sign-in revokes every other user's sessions.
TTL multiplied by 1000: cached 404 suggestions live ~16.7 hours instead of 60 s and show ended events.
Dropped end anchor: any path containing a dot followed by alphanumerics is treated as an asset probe and gets no suggestions.
Whitespace-only secrets no longer count as missing, so readiness stays green with a blank secret.
Reconstructed URI now includes the query string, so credentials in query parameters reach logs.
Record id 0 is admitted although serial ids start at 1.
Fold preference inverted: single events resolve to the earlier occurrence and series to the later one.
The archive page no longer filters unrenderable windows, so one poison row 500s the whole archive.
A 429 from Discord now marks the widget down and flips every visitor to the static fallback.
featuredImageAllowed no longer refuses userinfo URLs, so legacy rows with credentials render.
The single-use journey check is dropped from the OAuth callback, so a replayed callback is accepted.
A whitespace-only bot token is no longer treated as blank, so sign-in calls Discord with an unusable token.
`--target staging` now satisfies the production guard, so an erase can run against a production connection string.
The in-flight guard is dropped, so every request while the verdict is stale starts its own Discord probe.

seeds.old: if (cache?.source === source && Date.now() < cache.expiresAt) return cache.value;
seeds.desc: The cache no longer checks which database source filled it, so a binding change serves another source's rows.
The largest permitted occurrence count is now refused.
